stated: Transform how people travel by creating new cycling and walking networks with a new nationwide active travel strategy. Give more of the roads budget to local councils to maintain existing roads, pavements and cycleways, including repairing potholes.

source.quote: Transform how people travel by creating new cycling and walking networks with a new nationwide active travel strategy. Give more of the roads budget to local councils to maintain existing roads, pavements and cycleways, including repairing potholes.

bearing_set.reason: Shifting journeys from cars to cycling/walking directly reduces transport emissions and roadside air pollution, the core O6 indicators; the scale of a nationwide network makes this non-negligible.

A successful modal shift from car use to cycling/walking would reduce household transport costs (fuel, insurance, vehicle maintenance), directly raising real disposable income — transport is a significant share of the UK household spending basket.

A population-level shift to walking and cycling raises physical activity, reducing chronic disease burden (cardiovascular, obesity, mental health) and thereby reducing NHS demand — the mechanism is well-evidenced in public health literature and moves waiting-time/capacity indicators.

Repairing potholes and maintaining pavements/cycleways reduces vehicle operating and repair costs for households and freight, improves journey reliability, and reduces congestion — concrete mechanisms moving productivity and real living-standards indicators.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the environmental effect (O6) is the primary design purpose; the public-health demand-reduction effect on the NHS (O3) is well-evidenced and non-negligible at scale; road-maintenance productivity gains (O13) are documentable via vehicle damage and logistics costs. Fiscal redistribution (roads budget to councils) is within-envelope reallocation without a stated net change — insufficient mechanism to pin to O12 without further detail.
